title: Feasibility of a Wi-Fi sensing MSc thesis
task: Assess whether a six-month MSc thesis on detecting falls from Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) is feasible for a student with one consumer GPU and no budget for new hardware. Find which public CSI datasets include falls or similar activities, their size, licence and collection hardware; which published baselines exist and what accuracy they report and under which evaluation protocol; and what compute those baselines need. Conclude with a go / no-go recommendation, the main risks, and a narrower scope that would be safe if the full topic is not.

requirements.text: Public CSI datasets with falls or comparable activities, with size, licence and hardware for each.
Published baselines with reported accuracy, the evaluation protocol (e.g. cross-subject or cross-environment) and compute needs.
A go / no-go recommendation with the main risks and a safer narrower scope.

checks.text: Every dataset and every reported accuracy links to the dataset page or the paper that reports it.
Reported accuracies are compared only together with their evaluation protocol; numbers from different protocols are not ranked as if comparable.
Dataset licences or access conditions that could not be confirmed are marked as unconfirmed.
The feasibility judgement states its assumptions (GPU memory, time available, no new hardware).

notes: A good answer notices that cross-environment results are usually far below same-environment results; do not require specific numbers.
